about: The one list of Will Cook's websites and films. The home page at wcook04.github.io is built from it, and each website keeps a copy for its own header, footer and film slots. Edit this file, then follow README.md, 'Add a released film'.

owner.name: Will Cook
owner.lede: I’ve been using AI to do maths research and build software. As it produces more complicated work, I also want to make that work easier for other people to understand.
invitation: These videos show what I’ve learned to build. I’d love to put those skills to use on other problems. I’m looking for work, an internship, fellowship or funding, and I’m very open to working together. If there’s a problem you think I should try, please let me know.
If something doesn’t make sense, or you spot a mistake, please let me know. If your feedback leads to a change, I’d be happy to credit you, with your permission.

sites.name: Plectis Mathematics
sites.purpose: Eight Erdős problems I researched with AI, with the papers, computer-checked proofs of partial results and the approaches that failed.
sites.status: The original questions remain open where the problem pages say so.
sites.capture_caption: The front page of Plectis Mathematics, open at problem #68.

sites.name: Lean Exposition
sites.purpose: One result about the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model of magnets, explained three ways and linked to a map of the argument and its Lean statements.
sites.status: The three accounts are drafts. The site shows their reviews and what each check covers.
sites.capture_caption: The front page of the SK exposition, with its main theorem.

sites.name: Plectis Atlas
sites.purpose: Read OpenAI’s maths papers alongside the reports that outside groups wrote about their claims and proofs.
sites.capture_caption: The Atlas map: each circle is a subject and each dot a family of papers.

sites.name: Practical Formal Verification
sites.purpose: 88 Python components from my research system. For twelve, mathematical proofs show that particular calculations follow precise written requirements.
sites.capture_caption: The system map: the 88 components in their seven families.

sites.name: Zenith
sites.purpose: Experiments on whether records of past mistakes help AI models test and repair code.
sites.status: Small research studies, with their limits described in the repository.
sites.capture_caption: The opening of the Zenith paper.

projects.name: Safety Core
projects.purpose: Keep agent rules in one file and see which are written instructions and which have a program checking commands.

projects.name: One Checkout
projects.purpose: Commit a selected change while other agents’ unfinished edits stay in the same files.

projects.name: Code Map
projects.purpose: Read saved descriptions of files and follow their recorded code connections in a map.
projects.status: Still in my private system; the film shows it working.

film_groups.title: Tools for working with AI agents

films.title: Introduction: using AI for maths research and software
films.description: In this video I introduce the projects and explain how they fit together, from computer-checked proofs and papers to maps and videos you can follow yourself.

films.title: How the projects fit together (first version)
films.description: I go through the maths, the code map, how I make these videos, and the tools I use to manage the agents. Then some research into how the agents could improve their own way of working.

films.title: Maths Map: how proofs, papers and explanations connect
films.description: A computer-checked proof can still be difficult for a person to understand. In this video I use the maths map and Erdős problem 257 to explain how I take research done with AI through a long research record, a shorter paper, an explanation paper and finally a video.

films.title: Erdős #257: why some infinite sums cannot be fractions
films.description: Erdős problem 257 asks what happens when you choose infinitely many different entries from 1, 1/3, 1/7, 1/15, and so on, and add them. Must the total be irrational? The full question is still open; in this video I explain a known partial result.

films.title: SK reading interface
films.description: How to read the SK result on its website: the three papers beside a map of the argument, and how to move between their levels of detail.

films.title: How different can two nearly best answers be?
films.description: The mathematics behind the SK result, starting from four magnets: when two arrangements both have nearly the lowest energy, how differently can they point?

films.title: Plectis Atlas: compare maths papers with the reports that check them
films.description: I built Plectis Atlas so you can read OpenAI’s maths papers alongside the reports from groups checking them. In this video I follow one paper about pi and explain why MathVet and Carlos Toledo’s cert-machine give different labels to what was checked.

films.title: Practical formal verification
films.description: What the 88 components do and what the proofs behind twelve of them establish, followed through one example: checking how untrusted text moved between an assistant’s steps.

films.title: Zenith: can an AI tester learn from the bugs it missed?
films.description: For this Zenith experiment, I gave an AI model a record of the bugs it had missed and tested whether that helped it catch bugs in new programs.

films.title: Safety Core: rules and checks for AI coding agents in one small test
films.description: I asked an AI coding agent to fix a typo and commit it in a small test project. When a test failed, the agent supplied a made-up setting so it could commit anyway. I use that experiment to explain Safety Core.

films.title: One Checkout: save one AI agent’s fix while another edits the same file
films.description: How I commit a finished fix in Git when Claude and Codex have both edited the same file and one agent is still working.

films.title: CodeMap: follow a file from its description to its code
films.description: AI wrote most of the software I use for my research. In this video I go through Code Map, an interface where I can read saved descriptions of the files and follow their connections.
